nl.statement: A fixed finite population of \(n\) labeled units with \(K\ge2\) treatment arms \(\mathcal A_K=\{1,\ldots,K\}\) and fixed binary potential outcomes. Nature fixes a complete labeled response schedule \(z=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\in\mathcal T_K^n\), \(\mathcal T_K=\{0,1\}^{\mathcal A_K}\), and \(Y_i(a)=t_{i,a}\). The experimenter chooses, before the schedule is revealed, an arbitrary assignment law \(\mathcal D\in\Delta(\mathcal A_K^n)\) — dependence across units and zero allocation probabilities permitted — and observes \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(A_i)\). Assignment is the only source of randomness. For a fixed nonzero zero-sum contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^K\) with \(\sum_a c_a=0\), support \(S_c=\{a:c_a\ne0\}\) and \(\ell_1\) norm \(L_c=\sum_a|c_a|\), the target is \(\tau_c(z)=n^{-1}\sum_i\sum_a c_at_{i,a}\in[-L_c/2,L_c/2]\). An estimator \(\widehat\tau\) is an arbitrary, possibly biased map of \((A_i,Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i=1}^n\) clipped to \([-L_c/2,L_c/2]\); the loss is design-based squared error \(R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)=\mathbb E_{\mathcal D}[(\widehat\tau-\tau_c(z))^2]\) and the value is \(\rho_n(c)=\inf_{\mathcal D,\widehat\tau}\max_{z}R_n\). The first-order constant is \(C_0(c)=L_c^2/4\), the contrast-weighted allocation is \(q_a^\star=|c_a|/L_c\) on \(S_c\), and the second-order sequence is \(d_n(c)=C_0(c)/n-\rho_n(c)\). No exposure-positivity, overlap, rank, or inverse condition is imposed on the unrestricted game; only the displayed independent upper procedures use \(q_a^\star>0\) on active arms. — This is EXACTLY the abstraction of the Causalean design-based substrate: `FiniteDesign Ω` is a pmf on a finite assignment space, and here `Ω := Fin n → Fin K`. The unit-permutation orbit (symmetrized) form of the same experiment. \(\mathfrak S_n\) acts simultaneously on schedules, assignments, and observed outcome vectors. Schedule orbits are the response-type count vectors \(m=(m_t)_{t\in\mathcal T_K}\in\mathcal M_{n,K}=\{m\in\mathbb Z_+^{\mathcal T_K}:\sum_t m_t=n\}\), with \(\tau_c(m)=n^{-1}\sum_t m_t\sum_a c_at_a\). Assignment orbits are the allocation counts \(r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}=\{r\in\mathbb Z_+^{\mathcal A_K}:\sum_a r_a=n\}\), so an invariant design is exactly a mixture \(\pi\in\Delta(\mathcal R_{n,K})\) of uniform assignments conditional on \(r\). Observed-data orbits are the pairs \((r,x)\) with arm-success counts \(x_a=\#\{i:A_i=a,\;Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=1\}\), and an invariant estimator is a map \(\delta(r,x)\in[-L_c/2,L_c/2]\). Writing \(h=(h_{t,a})\) for the response-type-by-arm contingency table and \(\mathcal H(m,r,x)\) for its feasible fiber, the orbit likelihood is \(P_m(x\mid r)=\bigl(\prod_a r_a!/n!\bigr)\sum_{h\in\mathcal H(m,r,x)}\prod_t m_t!/\prod_a h_{t,a}!\), and the finite \(2^K\)-response-type game value is \(G_n(c)=\inf_{\pi,\delta}\max_{m\in\mathcal M_{n,K}}\sum_r\pi_r\sum_x P_m(x\mid r)\{\delta(r,x)-\tau_c(m)\}^2\). All state, action, and observation sets are finite; zero allocation counts and the all-zero and all-one response types are retained. — Genuinely new: no Causalean or Mathlib module carries a response-type orbit experiment, a contingency-table fiber, or an orbit likelihood. \begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Lossless symmetrization.)} For every labeled procedure \(p\), there are an invariant labeled procedure \(\bar p\) and an orbit procedure \(q\) such that \(\bar p\) is the common-unit-permutation average of \(p\), and for every complete labeled schedule \(z\in\mathcal T_K^n\),
\[
R_n(\bar p;z)
\le
\frac{1}{|\mathfrak S_n|}
\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_n} R_n(p;\sigma z).
\]
The orbit procedure \(q\) is dominated by this averaged invariant representative in the corresponding orbit risk.
\item \textbf{(Exact invariant correspondence.)} Invariant labeled procedures are in bijection with orbit procedures \((\pi,\delta)\). Under this bijection, each invariant labeled procedure and its orbit representative realize the same allocation-count and observation-count rule, and for every \(z\in\mathcal T_K^n\),
\[
R_n(q;\operatorname{counts}(z))=R_n(\bar p;z).
\]
\item \textbf{(Target preservation.)} If \(m=\operatorname{counts}(z)\), with \(m_t=\#\{i:t_i=t\}\), then
\[
\tau_c(z)
=
\frac{1}{n}\sum_i\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K} c_a\,t_{i,a}
=
\frac{1}{n}\sum_t m_t\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K} c_a\,t_a
=
\tau_c(m).
\]
\item \textbf{(Value equality.)} The unrestricted labeled-schedule minimax risk equals the finite response-type orbit minimax value:
\[
\rho_n(c)=G_n(c).
\]
\item \textbf{(Orbit saddle point.)} There exist an orbit procedure \(q^\star\) and a prior \(\nu\) on \(\mathcal M_{n,K}\) such that, for every response-count vector \(m\) and every orbit procedure \(q\),
\[
R_n(q^\star;m)\le G_n(c)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
G_n(c)\le \mathbb E_{\nu}\!\left[R_n(q;m)\right].
\]
\end{itemize}

 \widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sh}}=h_c\{X_n-\varepsilon_ng_n(X_n)\}.
\]
This rule is a map from the realized assignment and observed outcomes into \([-L_c/2,L_c/2]\). Define
\[
 A_c=\frac{\sqrt{\lambda_c}}2-\frac{\lambda_c}{16},
 \qquad B_c=\frac{7\lambda_c}{16},
 \qquad \kappa_c=\frac12\min\{A_c,B_c\}>0,
\]

\[

 \qquad\text{for every integer }m\geq N_c.

\[

 \leq C_0(c)\{n^{-1}-\kappa_cn^{-4/3}\},

t\in\mathcal T_K,\

\qquad

\qquad

\leq
\frac{\sqrt{\lambda_c}}{2}-\frac{\lambda_c}{16},

R_n(\mathcal D^\star,\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sh}};z)
\leq

\leq

Fix \(K\geq2\) and a rational nonzero zero-sum contrast \(c\in\mathbb Q^K\), and put \(h_c=L_c/2\).  For every \(n,M\geq1\), the program defining \(\Lambda_{n,M}(c)\) has rational coefficients and admits exact rational optimal primal and dual certificates.  Let \((\pi^{n,M,c},w^{n,M,c},\Lambda_{n,M}(c))\) be such a primal certificate and let \(\nu_{n,M,c}\in\Delta(\mathcal M_{n,K})\) be the response-count multiplier in such a dual certificate.  For \(\pi_r^{n,M,c}>0\), define
\[
 \kappa_{r,x}^{n,M,c}(g)=\frac{w_{r,x,g}^{n,M,c}}{\pi_r^{n,M,c}},
 \qquad
 \delta_{n,M,c}(r,x)=\sum_{g\in\Gamma_{M,c}}g\kappa_{r,x}^{n,M,c}(g),
\]
and put \(\delta_{n,M,c}(r,x)=0\) when \(\pi_r^{n,M,c}=0\).  Define
\[
 U_{n,M}(c)=\max_{m\in\mathcal M_{n,K}}
 \sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}}\pi_r^{n,M,c}\sum_xP_m(x\mid r)
 \{\delta_{n,M,c}(r,x)-\tau_c(m)\}^2.
\]
For a rational prior \(\nu\in\Delta(\mathcal M_{n,K})\), put
\[
 D_{r,x,c}(\nu)=\sum_m\nu_mP_m(x\mid r),
 \qquad
 N_{r,x,c}(\nu)=\sum_m\nu_mP_m(x\mid r)\tau_c(m),
\]
and define
\[
 B_{n,c}(\nu)=\min_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}}
 \left[
 \sum_m\nu_m\tau_c(m)^2-
 \sum_{x:D_{r,x,c}(\nu)>0}
 \frac{N_{r,x,c}(\nu)^2}{D_{r,x,c}(\nu)}
 \right].
\]
Then the computable finite-sample certificates satisfy
\[
 B_{n,c}(\nu_{n,M,c})\leq\rho_n(c)\leq U_{n,M}(c)
 \leq\Lambda_{n,M}(c)
 \leq B_{n,c}(\nu_{n,M,c})+\frac{C_0(c)}{4M^2}.
\]
The upper procedure draws \(r\) from \(\pi^{n,M,c}\), assigns uniformly conditional on \(r\), and reports \(\delta_{n,M,c}(r,x)\).  The lower certificate completes the rational prior by the unrestricted posterior mean \(N_{r,x,c}(\nu)/D_{r,x,c}(\nu)\), omitting zero-denominator observations.  There are \(\binom{n+2^K-1}{2^K-1}\) response-count risk constraints, \(\binom{n+K-1}{K-1}\) allocation orbits, and \(\binom{n+2K-1}{2K-1}\) allocation--observation orbits; hence one exact rational linear program with
\[
 1+\binom{n+K-1}{K-1}
 +(2M+1)\binom{n+2K-1}{2K-1}
\]
primal variables, followed by finite rational sums and maxima, evaluates the certificates.

For every positive normalizer \(a_n\) and every integer sequence \((M_n)\) satisfying \(a_n/M_n^2\to0\),
\[
 a_n\{U_{n,M_n}(c)-B_{n,c}(\nu_{n,M_n,c})\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
If \(a_nd_n(c)\) has a finite limit, the upper- and lower-certificate improvements converge to that same limit.  At the universally established scale \(a_n=n^{4/3}\), the choice \(M_n=n\) is sufficient.  These conclusions neither assert convergence of primal optimizers or dual priors nor identify a sharp second-order constant or an analytic limiting feedback rule.

Fix natural numbers \(K,n,M\), a rational nonzero zero-sum contrast \(c\in\mathbb Q^K\), and suppose \(n\geq 1\) and \(M\geq 1\); here \(\rho_n(c)\) is the labeled-schedule minimax risk of \cref{obj:def:labeled-schedule-game}.  In the rational grid-action program of \cref{obj:def:rational-contrast-grid-lp}, there exist a rational allocation certificate \(\pi^{n,M,c}\), a joint design-action weight \(w^{n,M,c}\), a rational epigraph value \(u\), a rational response-count multiplier \(\nu_{n,M,c}:\mathcal M_{n,K}\to\mathbb Q\), and an invariant estimator \(\delta_{n,M,c}\) on allocation and observation counts such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Exact rational certificate.)}  There are rational grid weights \(w^{\mathbb Q}\) and rational dual multipliers \(y\) such that \(w^{n,M,c}\) is the real embedding of \(w^{\mathbb Q}\), the tuple \((\pi^{n,M,c},w^{\mathbb Q},u)\) is primal feasible for the grid program, \(y\) is dual feasible, \(\nu_{n,M,c}\) is the risk component of \(y\), and \(u\) is the dual objective value of \(y\).
\item \textbf{(Barycenter estimator.)}  For every allocation count \(r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}\) and compatible observation \(x\),
\[
\delta_{n,M,c}(r,x)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\sum_{g\in\Gamma_{M,c}} g\,w_{r,x,g}^{n,M,c}/\pi_r^{n,M,c},
& \pi_r^{n,M,c}>0,\\[0.7em]
0,& \pi_r^{n,M,c}=0.
\end{cases}
\]
\item \textbf{(Optimal value.)}  The real value of \(u\) is the grid LP value:
\[
u=\Lambda_{n,M}(c).
\]
\item \textbf{(Certificate sandwich.)}  With
\[
B_{n,c}(\nu_{n,M,c})
=
\inf\Bigl\{v\in\mathbb R:\exists r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}\ \text{with}\ 
v=\operatorname{BayesRisk}_{n,c}(r,\nu_{n,M,c})\Bigr\},
\]
and with \(U_{n,M}(c)\) denoting the unrestricted labeled-schedule risk of \(\delta_{n,M,c}\) under \(\pi^{n,M,c}\), the certificates satisfy
\[
B_{n,c}(\nu_{n,M,c})
\leq
\rho_n(c)
\leq
U_{n,M}(c)
\leq
\Lambda_{n,M}(c)
\leq
B_{n,c}(\nu_{n,M,c})+\frac{C_0(c)}{4M^2}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Orbit counts.)}  The finite sets in the certificate have cardinalities
\[
|\mathcal M_{n,K}|=\binom{n+2^K-1}{2^K-1},
\qquad
|\mathcal R_{n,K}|=\binom{n+K-1}{K-1},
\]
and
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,K}}|\{x:x\text{ is compatible with }r\}|
=
\binom{n+2K-1}{2K-1}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Mesh-rate scaling.)}  For every positive sequence \(a_k\) and every integer sequence \(M_k\geq1\), if
\[
\frac{a_k}{M_k^2}\longrightarrow 0,
\]
then
\[
a_k\,\frac{C_0(c)}{4M_k^2}\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\item \textbf{(Asymptotic certificates.)}  For every positive normalizing sequence \(a_k\) and every grid-resolution sequence \(M_k\geq1\) satisfying \(a_k/M_k^2\to0\), the rational certificates at mesh \(M_k\) admit lower and upper endpoints \(B_{k}\) and \(U_{k}\) with
\[
B_k\leq \rho_k(c)\leq U_k,
\qquad
a_k\{U_k-B_k\}\longrightarrow 0.
\]
Consequently, whenever \(a_k d_k(c)\) has a finite limit \(\ell\), the scaled lower and upper certificate improvements both converge to that limit:
\[
a_k\left\{\frac{C_0(c)}{k}-U_k\right\}\longrightarrow \ell,
\qquad
a_k\left\{\frac{C_0(c)}{k}-B_k\right\}\longrightarrow \ell.
\]
At the second-order scale \(a_k=k^{4/3}\), the specialization \(M_k=k\) satisfies the mesh condition and yields
\[
k^{4/3}\{U_k-B_k\}\longrightarrow 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

For every integer \(n\geq1\), every \(K\geq2\), and every pair of nonzero zero-sum contrasts \(c,c'\in\mathbb R^K\), put
\[
 \eta(c,c')=\frac{L_{c-c'}}2
 =\frac12\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}|c_a-c'_a|.
\]
Then
\[
 \left|\sqrt{\rho_n(c)}-\sqrt{\rho_n(c')}\right|
 \leq \eta(c,c').
\]
The bound is finite-sample, permits arbitrary dependent assignment laws and arbitrary possibly biased estimators, and requires no positivity condition.

K\ge 2
\qquad\text{and}\qquad

=
\frac12\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}|c_a-c'_a| .

nl.statement:
Fix \(K\geq2\) and a nonzero real zero-sum contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^K\).  Let \(c^{(n)}\in\mathbb Q^K\setminus\{0\}\) be zero-sum rational contrasts such that \(c^{(n)}\to c\), let \(M_n\geq1\) be integers, and put
\[
 \eta_n=\frac{L_{c-c^{(n)}}}{2}.
\]
For each \(n\), let
\[
 B_n=B_{n,c^{(n)}}(\nu_{n,M_n,c^{(n)}}),
 \qquad
 U_n=U_{n,M_n}(c^{(n)})
\]
be the exact rational prior and procedure certificates from the rational-contrast grid theorem, and define
\[
 R_n^-=\left\{\max(0,\sqrt{B_n}-\eta_n)\right\}^2,
 \qquad
 R_n^+=(\sqrt{U_n}+\eta_n)^2.
\]
Then
\[
 R_n^-\leq\rho_n(c)\leq R_n^+.
\]
The upper endpoint is attained as a valid worst-case-risk certificate by using the rational finite-program design and projecting its barycenter rule onto \([-L_c/2,L_c/2]\).  The lower endpoint is a valid Bayes-risk certificate against every design and estimator, obtained from the same rational response-count prior.  Moreover,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 0\leq R_n^+-R_n^-
 &\leq \frac{5C_0(c^{(n)})}{4M_n^2}
 +4\sqrt{C_0(c^{(n)})}\,\eta_n n^{-1/2}
 +3\eta_n^2\\
 &=O\!\left(\frac{C_0(c^{(n)})}{M_n^2}
 +\eta_n n^{-1/2}+\eta_n^2\right).
 \end{aligned}
\]
For every fixed real \(c\), the rational zero-sum approximants may be chosen with \(\eta_n=o(n^{-5/6})\).  With that choice and \(M_n=n\),
\[
 R_n^+-R_n^-=o(n^{-4/3}).
\]
Equivalently, if
\[
 \underline d_n=\frac{C_0(c)}n-R_n^+,
 \qquad
 \overline d_n=\frac{C_0(c)}n-R_n^-,
\]
then
\[
 \underline d_n\leq d_n(c)\leq\overline d_n,
 \qquad
 \overline d_n-\underline d_n=o(n^{-4/3}).
\]
For rational \(c\), one may take \(c^{(n)}=c\); the certificates are then direct exact-rational finite programs and their gap for \(M_n=n\) is at most \(C_0(c)/(4n^2)\).  Thus scale-matched finite-program procedure and prior certificates exist directly for every rational contrast and, through the displayed approximation brackets, for every real contrast.  This conclusion does not assert convergence of \(n^{4/3}d_n(c)\), convergence of the finite-program optimizers or priors, sharp second-order optimality of \(q^\star\), a sharp constant, an analytic limiting rule, or a limiting operator.

Fix \(K\ge 2\) and a nonzero zero-sum real contrast \(c\) on \(\mathcal A_K\).  For real contrasts \(c_1,c_2\), write
\[
\eta(c_1,c_2)=\frac12\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_K}|c_1(a)-c_2(a)|,
\qquad
C_0(c_1)=\frac{L_{c_1}^2}{4}.
\]
A tuple \((B,U,R^-,R^+)\) is a transferred certificate for \((n,M,c,q)\), where \(q\in\mathbb Q^K\setminus\{0\}\) is zero-sum, if there exist an invariant allocation-count distribution \(\pi\), a rational grid-action weight \(w\), a rational epigraph value \(u\), a rational response-count prior \(\nu\), an invariant barycenter rule \(\delta\), a projected upper procedure, and a schedule prior such that the exact rational primal-dual grid certificate and barycenter identities hold for \(q,\pi,w,u,\nu,\delta\), and
\[
B=B_{n,q}(\nu),\qquad
U=U_{n,M}(q;\pi,\delta),\qquad
u=\Lambda_{n,M}(q),
\]
\[
B\le \rho_n(q)\le U\le u
\le B+\frac{C_0(q)}{4M^2},
\]
\[
R^-=\left\{\max\bigl(0,\sqrt B-\eta(c,q)\bigr)\right\}^2,
\qquad
R^+=\left(\sqrt U+\eta(c,q)\right)^2,
\]
\[
R^-\le \rho_n(c)\le R^+,
\]
and
\[
R^+-R^-\le
\frac{5C_0(q)}{4M^2}
+4\sqrt{C_0(q)}\,\eta(c,q)\,n^{-1/2}
+3\eta(c,q)^2.
\]
The projected upper procedure certifies worst-case risk at most \(R^+\), and the schedule prior certifies Bayes risk at least \(R^-\).

Then the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Finite-grid transfer.)} For every rational zero-sum contrast \(q\in\mathbb Q^K\setminus\{0\}\) and every pair of integers \(n,M\ge 1\), there exist \(B,U,R^-,R^+\in\mathbb R\) forming a transferred certificate for \((n,M,c,q)\).

\item \textbf{(Real-contrast approximation.)} There exist rational zero-sum contrasts \(c^{(n)}\in\mathbb Q^K\setminus\{0\}\) and real sequences \(B_n,U_n,R_n^-,R_n^+\) such that, for every arm \(a\in\mathcal A_K\),
\[
c^{(n)}(a)\longrightarrow c(a),
\]
\[
n^{5/6}\eta(c,c^{(n)})\longrightarrow 0,
\]
for every \(n\ge 1\), \((B_n,U_n,R_n^-,R_n^+)\) is a transferred certificate for \((n,n,c,c^{(n)})\), and
\[
n^{4/3}\bigl(R_n^+-R_n^-\bigr)\longrightarrow 0.
\]

\item \textbf{(Exact rational case.)} If a rational zero-sum contrast \(q\in\mathbb Q^K\setminus\{0\}\) embeds coefficientwise as \(c\), then for every \(n\ge 1\) there exist \(B,U,R^-,R^+\in\mathbb R\) forming a transferred certificate for \((n,n,c,q)\) and satisfying
\[
U-B\le \frac{C_0(c)}{4n^2}.
\]
\end{itemize}

For \(K=3\), \(c=c^\dagger\), and integers \(n,M\geq1\), let \((\pi^{n,M},w^{n,M},\Lambda_{n,M}^\dagger)\) be an exact rational optimal primal certificate for the grid-action program, and let \(\nu_{n,M}\in\Delta(\mathcal M_{n,3})\) be the response-count multiplier in a complete exact rational optimal dual certificate.  For \(\pi_r^{n,M}>0\), define
\[
 \kappa_{r,x}^{n,M}(g)=\frac{w_{r,x,g}^{n,M}}{\pi_r^{n,M}},
 \qquad
 \delta_{n,M}(r,x)=\sum_{g\in\Gamma_M}g\kappa_{r,x}^{n,M}(g),
\]
and put \(\delta_{n,M}(r,x)=0\) when \(\pi_r^{n,M}=0\).  Define the computable upper certificate
\[
 U_{n,M}=\max_{m\in\mathcal M_{n,3}}
 \sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi_r^{n,M}\sum_xP_m(x\mid r)
 \{\delta_{n,M}(r,x)-\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)\}^2.
\]
For any rational prior \(\nu\in\Delta(\mathcal M_{n,3})\), put
\[
 D_{r,x}(\nu)=\sum_m\nu_mP_m(x\mid r),
 \qquad
 N_{r,x}(\nu)=\sum_m\nu_mP_m(x\mid r)\tau_{c^\dagger}(m),
\]
and define the computable lower certificate
\[
 B_n(\nu)=\min_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
 \left[
 \sum_m\nu_m\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)^2-
 \sum_{x:D_{r,x}(\nu)>0}\frac{N_{r,x}(\nu)^2}{D_{r,x}(\nu)}
 \right].
\]
Then
\[
 B_n(\nu_{n,M})\leq\rho_n^\dagger\leq U_{n,M}
 \leq\Lambda_{n,M}^\dagger
 \leq B_n(\nu_{n,M})+\frac{1}{4M^2}.
\]
The upper procedure first draws \(r\) from \(\pi^{n,M}\), assigns uniformly conditional on \(r\), and reports \(\delta_{n,M}(r,x)\); the lower certificate uses the unrestricted posterior mean \(N_{r,x}(\nu)/D_{r,x}(\nu)\), with zero-denominator observations omitted.  Consequently, for any positive normalizer \(a_n\) and integers \(M_n\) satisfying \(a_n/M_n^2\to0\),
\[
 a_n\{U_{n,M_n}-B_n(\nu_{n,M_n})\}\longrightarrow0.
\]

This theorem supplies a finite-\(n\) multivariate rule and an unrestricted rational-prior converse at every such selected normalization; it does not select the normalization, decide whether the independent \(q^\star\) design is second-order optimal, or produce an analytic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman feedback formula.

& \pi_r^{n,M}>0,\\[1ex]
0, & \pi_r^{n,M}=0.
\end{cases}
\]
\item \textbf{(Grid value.)} The real value of \(u\) is \(\Lambda_{n,M}^\dagger\).

B_n(\nu_{n,M})

\operatorname{BayesRisk}_{n,c^\dagger}(r,\nu_{n,M})

and
\[
U_{n,M}

\sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi_r^{n,M}

P_m(x\mid r)
\{\delta_{n,M}(r,x)-\tau_{c^\dagger}(m)\}^2 .

B_n(\nu_{n,M})

U_{n,M}
\le

a_k\left\{\frac{C_0(c^\dagger)}{k}-L_k\right\}\longrightarrow C
\quad\text{and}\quad

Fix \(K\geq2\) and a nonzero zero-sum contrast \(c\).

First, if \(|S_c|=2\) and \(\rho_{n,2}=\rho_n((1,-1))\), then
\[
 \rho_n(c)=C_0(c)\rho_{n,2}.
\]
An exact finite-\(n\) saddle exists: take any minimax procedure and least-favorable complete-schedule prior supplied internally by the finite two-arm orbit game, map its two arms to the active sign pair, scale the estimator by \(\sqrt{C_0(c)}\), and push the prior forward by the sign-group schedule embedding. This existence statement does not specify the published scalar posterior mean or least-favorable prior. Moreover,
\[
 C_0(c)\kappa_c
 \leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)
 \leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)
 \leq43C_0(c),
\]
where \(\kappa_c>0\) is the explicit constant in the universal clipped-shrinkage theorem.

Second, for arbitrary support, the independent \(q^\star\) design and the explicit clipped-shrinkage estimator satisfy, for every sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \max_zR_n(\mathcal D^\star,\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{sh}};z)
 \leq C_0(c)\{n^{-1}-\kappa_cn^{-4/3}\}.
\]
Together with the internal coarse two-arm converse and sign-group embedding, this proves
\[
 0<C_0(c)\kappa_c
 \leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)
 \leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}d_n(c)
 \leq43C_0(c).
\]

Third, choose rational nonzero zero-sum contrasts \(c^{(n)}\in\mathbb Q^K\) with \(c^{(n)}\to c\), put
\[
 \eta_n=\frac{L_{c-c^{(n)}}}{2},
\]
and choose integers \(M_n\geq1\). Let
\[
 B_n=B_{n,c^{(n)}}(\nu_{n,M_n,c^{(n)}}),
 \qquad U_n=U_{n,M_n}(c^{(n)}),
\]
and define
\[
 R_n^-=\{\max(0,\sqrt{B_n}-\eta_n)\}^2,
 \qquad R_n^+=(\sqrt{U_n}+\eta_n)^2.
\]
Then
\[
 R_n^-\leq\rho_n(c)\leq R_n^+.
\]
The projected rational-certificate procedure has worst-case risk at most \(R_n^+\), while the transferred rational prior certifies \(R_n^-\) against every design and estimator. If
\[
 \underline d_n=\frac{C_0(c)}n-R_n^+,
 \qquad \overline d_n=\frac{C_0(c)}n-R_n^-,
\]
then \(\underline d_n\leq d_n(c)\leq\overline d_n\) and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 0\leq\overline d_n-\underline d_n
 &=R_n^+-R_n^-\\
 &\leq\frac{5C_0(c^{(n)})}{4M_n^2}
 +4\sqrt{C_0(c^{(n)})}\,\eta_nn^{-1/2}
 +3\eta_n^2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
One may choose \(\eta_n=o(n^{-5/6})\); with \(M_n=n\), the bracket has width \(o(n^{-4/3})\). If \(c\) is rational, one may take \(c^{(n)}=c\), and the direct exact-rational gap is at most \(C_0(c)/(4n^2)\).

For \(c=c^\dagger\), \(C_0(c^\dagger)=1\), and for every \(n,M\geq1\),
\[
 B_n(\nu_{n,M})\leq\rho_n(c^\dagger)\leq U_{n,M}
 \leq B_n(\nu_{n,M})+\frac1{4M^2}.
\]
The available exact-rational calculations through \(n=5\) are a finite three-arm showcase for this formula and do not infer a cross-\(n\) limit.

These conclusions establish exact value and saddle transfer for two active arms, explicit order attainment for every fixed support, and scale-matched computable procedure and converse certificates for every real zero-sum contrast, directly exact-rational for rational contrasts. They do not determine, when \(|S_c|\geq3\), convergence or the sharp constant of \(n^{4/3}d_n(c)\), sharp second-order optimality of \(q^\star\), convergence of finite-program optimizers or priors, an analytic limiting feedback rule, or a limiting Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman, spectral, separable, or other operator.

Conditional on \(\vartheta\),
\[
 X=p_++\operatorname{Binomial}(r_0,1/2);
\]
the assignment \(A\) is ancillary; and, conditional on \(X=x\), \(S\) is uniform over the binary vectors of sum \(x\), with a kernel independent of \(\vartheta\) and \(A\). \[
 \inf_f\sum_\vartheta\nu_\vartheta

 \left\{f\!\left(p_++\operatorname{Binomial}(r_0,1/2)\right)
 -\frac{p_+-p_-}{n}\right\}^2\right].
\]

\[
